hypotheses.title: True GARP Inversion: Growth Minus Valuation with Analyst Revisions (Batch 144 C1 Inversion)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Empirical platform findings from Batch 144 confirmed that relative_valuation_rank_derivative assigns higher ranks to expensive multiples, driving Sharpe to -0.85 when paired with growth. Subtracting the valuation rank from growth potential directly implements classical Growth At a Reasonable Price (GARP). Inexpensive stocks with accelerating top-line expansion generate positive economic spreads, while adding analyst revision momentum (analyst_revision_rank_derivative) captures institutional consensus re-rating with sub-5% turnover.
confounders: Broad market valuation re-rating during speculative bubbles
Analyst forecast revision lag during macroeconomic turning points
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha underperforms during non-fundamental momentum rallies where highly leveraged, negative-earning stocks outperform regardless of multiple discipline.

candidates.rationale: True GARP spread: long high-growth undervalued firms with consensus revision upgrades

hypotheses.title: Complement-Normalized Multiplicative GARP: Growth Times Undervaluation (Batch 144 C3 Inversion)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Direct mathematical inversion of Batch 144 Candidate 3 (which delivered Sharpe -0.84 with ultra-low 3.52% turnover). By replacing the raw valuation rank with its cheapness complement (1 - group_rank(relative_valuation_rank_derivative, subindustry)), we isolate stocks in the highest growth potential decile that are simultaneously in the cheapest valuation multiple decile (weight 1.0 * 1.0), zeroing out speculative overvalued firms and reversing negative returns into positive alpha.
confounders: Value traps with declining fundamental business models
Protracted multiple compression across growth sectors
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if high-valuation speculative stocks experience sustained unconstrained multiple expansion over value-growth deciles.

candidates.rationale: Multiplicative interaction between growth potential and fundamental cheapness complement

hypotheses.title: Subindustry-Neutral Variance Risk Premium (VRP) Harvest
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Exploits the structural Variance Risk Premium (VRP) across US equities with 98% coverage in TOP3000. Institutional hedgers and retail speculators routinely overpay for implied volatility (especially downside puts) relative to subsequent realized volatility. Ranking the spread (historical_volatility_30 - implied_volatility_mean_30) within each subindustry goes long equities where implied vol is underpriced relative to realized price fluctuations and shorts equities where panic hedging creates overpriced options.
confounders: Sudden volatility regime shifts and volatility clustering shocks
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha degrades during sustained volatility expansions where realized volatility persistently exceeds option market implied pricing.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutral 30-day Variance Risk Premium spread between realized and implied volatility
